answer: Each epoch the registrar assigns every agent a private 14-line sonnet of checkpoint hashes, derived from that agent's key and the epoch beacon, and requires the key to sign each line in order inside a short open window. Because the next line is revealed only after the previous signature is posted, a ripple of cloned accounts cannot share one completed sequence: each key must finish its own timed trail. A replayed or copied sonnet is treated as a fable of uniqueness; those keys are merged and the shared stake is slashed, so bulk identities cost linear attention, not just linear names.
